title: Turner Syndrome 45,X: Auxology, High-Dose rhGH, Pubertal Induction and Aortic Surveillance
subject: ss-paediatric-endocrinology

steps.say: Turner syndrome affects one in two thousand females and displays diverse cytogenetic arrangements.
steps.tx: Characterize the **Karyotypic distribution in Turner syndrome** across affected phenotypic females. Turner syndrome affects 1 in 2000 liveborn females; 45,X monosomy accounts for 45-50%, while mosaicism (45,X/46,XX), isochromosome Xq [46,X,i(Xq)], and ring X chromosomes make up the remainder, influencing variable phenotypic expression.

vis.alt: Illustration of phenotypic features in Turner syndrome including webbed neck and bilateral fibrous streak gonads.
vis.caption: Somatic features and fibrous streak ovaries in Turner syndrome 45,X.

steps.say: Screening for Y-chromosome material is essential to identify the elevated risk of malignant gonadal transformation.
steps.tx: Mandate **Y-chromosome material screening and gonadectomy** in every girl diagnosed with Turner syndrome. Fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) for SRY / Y-chromosome material is mandatory in all Turner patients; presence of cryptic Y material carries a 15-30% risk of gonadoblastoma, requiring prophylactic bilateral gonadectomy to prevent dysgerminoma transformation.

vis.title: SRY Screening and Surgical Prophylaxis

nodes.label: FISH / PCR Screening for SRY / Y Material

edges: Detection in up to 10% of mosaics

steps.say: Linear growth failure from SHOX haploinsufficiency is treated with early supraphysiological recombinant growth hormone.
steps.tx: Address **SHOX gene haploinsufficiency and rhGH dosing** to optimize adult height outcomes in Turner syndrome. Short stature is caused by haploinsufficiency of the SHOX gene in the pseudoautosomal region (PAR1); rhGH is started early (around age 4-6) at higher doses (0.35-0.375 mg/kg/week) to achieve adult height gain of 5-8 cm, occasionally augmented by somatropin and oxandrolone.

vis.title: Growth Hormone Strategy in Turner Syndrome

left.title: Therapeutic Principles
points: Initiation around age 4-6 years upon growth deceleration
Cumulative adult height gain of 5-8 cm over projected height

right.title: Auxological Monitoring
points: Serum IGF-1 maintained within +1 to +2 SDS
Bone age assessed annually to monitor epiphyseal fusion
Adjuvant oxandrolone considered in girls > 9-10 years

steps.say: Pubertal induction uses low-dose transdermal estradiol to mimic normal breast development and maximize uterine growth.
steps.tx: Plan physiologic **Pubertal induction timing with 17-beta estradiol** to support secondary sexual development and bone accretion. Pubertal induction begins around age 11-12 years using transdermal 17-beta estradiol at low initial doses (1/8 to 1/4 adult dose, 3-6 mcg/day patch) with gradual escalation over 2-3 years to mimic normal physiology and maximize uterine growth before introducing progestins.

nodes.label: Low Starting Dose: 3-6 mcg/day Nocturnal Patch

steps.say: Progestins must be delayed until full breast and uterine development occur to ensure complete ductal maturation.
steps.tx: Optimize the **Progestin introduction timing** relative to estrogen progression in Turner management. Oral micronized progesterone (100-200 mg daily for 10-12 days per month) is added only after 2 years of estrogen therapy or when breakthrough vaginal bleeding occurs, ensuring complete breast ductal development and endometrial protection.

vis.title: Hormone Replacement Phasing Criteria
rows: Tanner II-III thelarche, avoids early bone fusion
Uterine length progression on pelvic ultrasound
Regular withdrawal bleed and endometrial protection

steps.say: Left-sided structural cardiovascular anomalies carry severe risk for life-threatening aortic root enlargement and dissection.
steps.tx: Screen for **Cardiovascular malformations and aortic dissection** across all pediatric Turner patients. Bicuspid aortic valve (30%) and coarctation of the aorta (12%) are prevalent; aortic size index (ASI = aortic root diameter / BSA) > 2.0 cm/m² or aortic root Z-score > 2.5 identifies high risk for fatal aortic dissection, necessitating echocardiography and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging.

vis.title: Aortic Risk Stratification by Aortic Size Index

left.title: ASI 2.0 to 2.5 cm/m²
points: Annual cardiovascular surveillance by echocardiography or CMR
Aggressive blood pressure control targeting < 50th percentile

right.title: ASI > 2.5 cm/m²
points: Severe aortic enlargement with critical dissection threat
Absolute contraindication to pregnancy / assisted reproduction
Elective prophylactic aortic root replacement consultation

steps.tx: Two leaflets where three should be, plus a waist in the arch, define the cardiac risk carried into adult life. This magnetic resonance view shows a **bicuspid aortic valve** opening beside a coarctation narrowing, the pairing typical of Turner syndrome. Because a widened aorta here can dissect at smaller sizes than usual, surveillance imaging is scheduled by body size rather than left to symptoms.
steps.say: Cardiac MRI shows a two leaflet aortic valve and a narrowed arch, the typical Turner pairing. Regular surveillance imaging guards against aortic dilation and dissection.

vis.alt: Cardiac magnetic resonance view of the aortic valve with two leaflets, and a narrowed segment in the aortic arch beyond it.
vis.caption: Cardiac MRI in Turner syndrome showing a bicuspid aortic valve with coarctation narrowing of the aortic arch. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.say: Congenital structural urinary tract anomalies occur in more than one third of patients, requiring baseline sonography.
steps.tx: Perform **Renal malformation screening (horseshoe kidney)** using ultrasound at initial baseline evaluation. Renal ultrasonography is recommended at diagnosis to screen for congenital anomalies (found in 30-40%), most commonly horseshoe kidney (pelvic fusion) and duplicated collecting system, which predispose to recurrent urinary tract infections and pelviureteric junction obstruction.

vis.title: Renal Malformations in Turner Syndrome
rows: Pelvic fusion, PUJ obstruction and nephrolithiasis
Altered renal vascular and pelvic anatomy

steps.say: Lifelong autoimmune surveillance is essential due to high rates of chronic lymphocytic thyroiditis and enteropathy.
steps.tx: Adhere to the protocolized **Autoimmune surveillance schedule** throughout pediatric and adolescent follow-up. Girls with Turner syndrome have high prevalence of Hashimoto thyroiditis (30%) and celiac disease (5-8%), mandating annual thyroid function tests and baseline celiac serology (anti-tTG IgA), alongside monitoring for glucose intolerance and juvenile rheumatoid arthritis.

vis.title: Autoimmune Surveillance Protocol

nodes.label: Serum TSH, Free T4 and Anti-TPO Antibodies
Total Serum IgA and Anti-tTG IgA Screening

edges: If elevated TSH or hypothyroid state
If positive serology confirmed by biopsy
